Prevention: Nematodes are tiny worm-like animals which live in the soil and burrow into roots which cause damage to crops.
They are not visible to the naked eye.
Use clean planting materials e.g. clean suckers or tissue cultured bananas.
Before planting, solarise the soil using a polythene sheet (gauge 150) for at least a month during hot weather.
Fallow the land prior to planting for a period of at least 6-12 months to reduce potential nematode populations.
Apply heavy mulch with organic waste e.g. maize stover, grass or another non-banana plant.
If the field has been previously infested, remove as many weeds as possible.
If nematodes have been a previous problem, plough deeply in hot weather, before planting, to expose nematodes to heat and kill them.
Rotate crops with legumes (e.g. beans, peas), brassicas (e.g. cabbages, kales), rape and/or marigold flowers ( Tagetes spp.) for at least 2 years.
Avoid planting spinach, capsicum, eggplant or citrus during this period.
Alternatively rotate with paddy rice to flood field and reduce populations.
Avoid movement of planting materials and soil as well as run off of irrigation water to prevent spread of nemtaodes.
They can only move a few metres in the soil per year.
Clean farm tools and equipment after use.
Monitoring: Regularly monitor for symptoms both above and below ground.
Single stunted plants in a smallholding or spots of stunted plants in larger plantations.
Plant toppling (due to loss of anchoring roots).
Wilting of plants even if there is adequate water supply.
Uniform yellowing or chlorosis of the lower leaves even if soil is adequately fertilized.
Reduced number and size of leaves.
Brown lesions and clumping of side roots.
